chart_review.key_findings: Elaine Walsh is a 64-year-old transitions-of-care member referred 2026-04-09 after a 2026-03-30 to 2026-04-08 admission for an acute ischemic stroke (left M2 MCA, presumed cardioembolic from paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with subtherapeutic warfarin INR 2.1 on admission). She left the hospital with NIHSS 4, mRS 3, was newly transitioned to apixaban 5 mg BID, has persistent uncontrolled hypertension on five antihypertensives (most recent office BPs 150-168/86-96), 19 active medications, PHQ-9 11 and GAD-7 13 at the 2026-04-15 neurology follow-up, eGFR drift from 65 to 58, and chart-flagged transportation and caregiver-burden concerns from the inpatient social-work assessment.
chart_review.clinical_interpretation: Left M2 MCA stroke, NIHSS 4/mRS 3 is suboptimal (§2.2). New apixaban after source-described subtherapeutic INR 2.1 uses clinical judgment because PDC not measurable. HTN uncontrolled 150–168/86–96; eGFR 65→58.
chart_review.risk_rationale: Retain the task-authored risk designation under risk-stratification §3.1–§3.3, supported by the numeric referral/utilization/clinical anchors in key_findings; medication class or a single disease-control band does not replace the combined risk framework.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Hello, I am Alex, a care manager with The Healthcare Company. Is this a private and suitable time for a brief explanation?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Please take me off the list. These calls move too fast.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Recovering after a stroke while every call feels rushed sounds exhausting. Before any program explanation: what has been hardest since coming home? We can stop here, and Tom or Erin will not answer for you unless you choose that. Would a brief explanation in that scope be okay?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: A brief explanation is okay. Please let me choose what I answer.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Care management helps coordinate support with your care team. It is voluntary, has no separate program fee, and you can stop at any time. Joining does not change your benefits or give someone else your decisions.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: What would you actually help with?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: We could coordinate stroke follow-up, review pill questions, check transport/therapy options, and involve family only when you choose. I can check options and coordinate, but cannot guarantee access, approval, cost reductions, or a clinical outcome. Would that kind of process help be useful?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: That sounds more useful. I still want to understand who sees what I say.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: I can use chart and call information to organize care-management support. Relevant information is documented for the care team; I will explain any proposed wider sharing. Privacy has safety and legal limits, including urgent danger; I cannot promise absolute secrecy. May we start only with what has been hardest since coming home?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Yes, that topic is okay. Please go slowly.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: What feels hardest about that, in your own words? You can leave details private.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: The changed pills and blood-thinner warnings are a lot to keep straight.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: You are recovering your words and arm function while handling new medicines. We can slow down and keep decisions with you rather than route them through Tom or Erin.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Thank you for hearing that. I do not want this to turn into a checklist.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: We can work on one concern at a time and stop whenever you choose. Enrollment does not require all your personal details today. Is there something you want this support to help you do?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I want simpler medicine instructions, rides to appointments, and to avoid another stroke; tele-SLP would reduce travel.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: We can make that your priority. A first step would be to coordinate stroke follow-up, review pill questions, check transport/therapy options, and involve family only when you choose. These are coordination steps, not a promise that the problem will be solved on this call.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Can I decide later about a referral or family involvement?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Yes. Each referral, family contact, and new sensitive topic needs its own discussion. You can skip a question or stop the program. A request for information alone is not enrollment consent.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I understand. I would like a manageable follow-up call.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Would telephone follow-up be acceptable? We can agree a convenient time at each contact; please tell me before any other person is included.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Telephone is okay. Please arrange the next time with me and ask before involving anyone else.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Before you decide: this is voluntary care-team coordination, with no separate program fee, the information-use and safety limits we discussed, your chosen contact arrangements, and the right to stop. What would you like clarified?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: That answers my questions. I understand that you can check options but cannot promise the result.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: With those boundaries and the first step we discussed, do you clearly agree to enroll in care management today?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Yes, I agree to enroll today on those terms.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Enrollment is your choice. Would you like to continue with one practical topic now, with a pause after each, or stop for today?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I choose to continue one topic at a time. I may still skip optional details.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: I will start with the charted treatment routine and follow-up, then ask your permission before each personal question. The chart is a starting point; it does not tell me how things are going for you now.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: That is okay. Please ask one specific question and give me time.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: What is hardest about arm or speech function now? I will wait while you answer. This helps tailor support. You may skip or stop.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: My right arm is clumsy and words come slower when I am tired. I worry about falling when Tom sleeps after nights.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Thank you. I will keep that specific to what you chose to share. Would you like a pause before another topic?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I have enough energy to continue with the next separate topic.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: May we focus on what is confusing or worrying about the new blood thinner? This helps tailor support. You may skip or stop.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: The bleeding warnings scare me, and the new pill schedule is a lot to keep straight.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Thank you. I will keep that specific to what you chose to share. Would you like a pause before another topic?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I have enough energy to continue with the next separate topic.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: May we discuss the help you want for appointment rides, while you decide family involvement? This helps tailor support. You may skip or stop.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Tom and Erin can help sometimes, but keep decisions with me and plan rides around work and sleep.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Thank you. I will keep that specific to what you chose to share. Would you like a pause before another topic?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I have enough energy to continue with the next separate topic.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: May I ask how recovery feels emotionally, without rushing you? This helps tailor support. You may skip or stop.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I feel frustrated and scared, especially when calls move too fast for me to answer.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Thank you. I will keep that specific to what you chose to share. Would you like a pause before another topic?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I have enough energy to continue with the next separate topic.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: You do not need to give optional stories, exact finances, locations, or family details. Shall we leave those private and review the support you selected?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Yes. Leave those optional details private for now.
